resolved_missing_files.description: Skeleton Jupyter notebook with 3 cells: (a) tiktoken tokenizer demo — tokenize a physics sentence and print token IDs and decoded tokens side-by-side; (b) count_tokens(prompt: str, model: str) -> int stub using tiktoken.encoding_for_model; (c) buggy OpenAI chat completions API call with a misspelled model name and temperature=2.0. Students must complete cell (b) and find/fix both bugs in cell (c), then verify the binding energy of iron-56.
resolved_missing_files.source_quote: The instructor pre-loads a skeleton Jupyter notebook into the course GitHub repository (path: exercises/week01/meeting1_token_explorer.ipynb).

resolved_missing_files.description: Python script ostensibly generated by Claude that computes and plots the first 5 energy levels and wavefunctions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. Contains exactly 5 planted bugs: (1) E_n = hbar*omega*n instead of hbar*omega*(n+0.5); (2) psi[1:N] off-by-one drops ground state; (3) hallucinated scipy.special.hermite_poly(n,x) API call; (4) wrong normalization divisor 1/sqrt(n!) instead of correct Hermite-Gauss formula; (5) plots psi instead of abs(psi)**2 for probability density.
resolved_missing_files.source_quote: Before class: the instructor prepares a Python script named week02_buggy_harmonic_oscillator.py (committed to the course repository)...

resolved_missing_files.description: Skeleton notebook with: (1) problem statement for a projectile motion simulator with linear drag (F_drag = -b*v) computing range, max height, and time of flight; (2) a pre-written pytest suite of 5 tests: test_vacuum_range (R = v0^2*sin(2*theta)/g), test_vacuum_max_height, test_drag_reduces_range, test_time_of_flight_positive, test_symmetry_broken_by_drag (optimal angle < 45 deg with drag); (3) three empty cells labeled 'Your AI Prompt', 'AI-Generated Code', and 'Test Results'.
resolved_missing_files.source_quote: Before class: the instructor commits a skeleton Jupyter notebook named week02_test_driven_skeleton.ipynb to the course repository.

resolved_missing_files.description: Pre-written Python script that fetches data from SIMBAD and the Materials Project, normalizes units, and writes a provenance JSON file. Contains exactly 3 planted failures: (a) a rate-limit exception silently swallowed by bare except, returning stale cache; (b) SIMBAD solar-luminosity values added directly to a column labeled L_SI without unit conversion (off by factor ~3.8e26); (c) missing .get() guard on response['band_gap'] causing KeyError on metallic compounds.
resolved_missing_files.source_quote: The instructor provides a pre-written Python script (multi_api_pipeline_broken.py, committed to the course repository before class)...
